(PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE A.Y. KOGJE)
1.

The present appeal is preferred by the appellant-State under Section 378 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 against judgment and order of acquittal dated 30.10.2002 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court No.2, Nadiad, District NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/466/2003 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/03/2026 undefined Kheda in Sessions case No. 155 of 1998.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court No.2, Nadiad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By the impugned judgment and order, the Sessions Court acquitted the respondents- accused for offence under Sections 376 read with Section 114 and Sections 506(2) read with Section 114 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The brief facts of the case are that the prosecutrix, who was a resident of the village Venikui, was acquainted with the accused persons as they used to visit the area where she resided.

It is alleged that for about two years prior to the lodging of the complaint, the accused persons took the prosecutrix to the fields near her house and committed sexual intercourse with her against her will and threatened her with dire consequences if she disclosed the same to anyone.

It is further alleged that due to the said act committed by the accused, the prosecutrix was impregnated and on 25.11.1997, when her mother noticed the sign of pregnancy, upon questioning, the prosecutrix disclosed the said facts to her mother.
Thereafter, her father was informed and a complaint came to be filed on 25.11.1997.

3. Learned APP appearing for the appellant-state has submitted that the order of acquittal passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court No.2, Nadiad, District Kheda in Sessions case No. 155 of 1998 is against law and evidence on record.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court No.2, Nadiad, District Kheda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/466/2003 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/03/2026 undefined 3.1.

It is submitted that the trial Court has failed to appreciate the documentary evidence produced vide Exh.24 as a reliable proof of the age of the prosecutrix, wherein the date of birth of the prosecutrix has been clearly mentioned i.e., 10.10.1981 and the prosecutrix was therefore a minor at the time of the incident.

3.2. It is also submitted that the trial Court has committed an error in discarding the evidence of the prosecutrix by giving importance to minor omissions and contradictions though the prosecutrix had clearly narrated the circumstances wherein the alleged incident took place.

3.3. It is further submitted that the prosecutrix had not disclosed about the incident to her parents as she had been threatened by the accused persons and therefore the delay in filing the complaint has been sufficiently explained.

4. As against this, learned Advocate on behalf of the respondents-accused supported the impugned judgment and order passed by the trial Court and has submitted that the trial Court has rightly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence on record and acquitted the accused persons.

It is further submitted that the prosecution has not adduced birth certificate or ossification report in order to establish NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/466/2003 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/03/2026 undefined that the prosecutrix was a minor at the time when the alleged incident took place and that the school record which is relied upon by the prosecution has not been proved through proper evidence.
4.2. It is further submitted that the evidence of the prosecutrix is unreliable as, in her deposition she has materially contradicted the allegations which were made by her in the complaint.

4.3. It is further submitted that the prosecutrix in her cross examination, has admitted that she had entered into a compromise with accused No.2 and had also expressed willingness to compromise with accused No.1 if she was paid monetary compensation, which makes her evidence unreliable.

5. The Court has considered the date of incident and registration of complaint, being 25.11.1997,
which is pre-POCSO Act.

Upon perusal of the record, it appears that in order to prove the case against the respondents-accused, the prosecution has examined the following witnesses:-

The prosecution has also brought on record the following documentary evidence :
 Sr. No. Particular   4. Medical-legal certificate of prosecutrix   5. Copy of entry no.96 made in the register of As 6.

It appears that the case of the prosecution rests upon the evidence of the prosecutrix being PW No.4, examined vide Exh.57 alongwith other documentary evidence to establish the age of the prosecutrix.
It is a settled position of law that the Court can base the conviction of the accused on the evidence of the prosecutrix in a rape case provided that it is found to be reliable and trustworthy.
However, the Court must exercise caution in cases where the evidence of the prosecutrix consists of material inconsistencies and is found to be unreliable.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/466/2003 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/03/2026 undefined 7.
In this regard, the Court has extensively perused the evidence of the victim being PW No.4 examined vide Exh.57.
At the time of recording of the evidence, the age of the victim is mentioned as 21 years and it has come on record that she has already married.

8. Upon perusal of the deposition of the prosecutrix, the evidence-in-chief itself would indicate that though the charge is claimed against two accused namely accused No.1-Jerabhai Lalabhai Thakor and accused No.2-Laalo @ Suresh Shanabhai Thakor, the witness has refused to attribute any role to accused No.2-Laalo @ Suresh and has in fact gone to the extent of deposing that she does not even know accused No.2-Laalo @ Suresh.

9. With regards to the incident which according to the prosecution is approximately 2 years prior to the registration of the F.I.R, the incident deposed to is of intercepting the victim by accused State Of Gujarat vs Jerabhai Lalabhai Thakore on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19238527/
4 No.1-Jerabhai and dragging her to an isolated place to commit rape and thereafter on many occasions, rape has been committed over the course of two years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the cross- examination of the prosecutrix with regards to the very first incident would indicate that she had not raised any alarm though the area from where she is allegedly dragged from was not an isolated area and was frequently visited by the ladies of the village NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/466/2003 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/03/2026 undefined for fetching water.

She has also deposed in her cross-examination that she had not sustained any injury on account of her alleged dragging of the victim by accused No.1-Jerabhai before commission of the offence and she has also deposed that she made no attempt to escape from the clutches of accused No.1-Jerabhai.

10. In the deposition of the prosecutrix, the Court has also come across the questions put to the witness victim about the settlement which has been arrived at which initially, in her deposition she has refused to answer but later on has clearly indicated that she has settled the matter outside the Court with accused No.2-Laalo @ Suresh and would have also settled the matter with accused No.1-Jerabhai, had he made offered some monetary compensation.

11. Therefore, upon considering the evidence of the prosecutrix, which does not inspire confidence and the trial Court has treated nature of evidence laid by the prosecutrix and put her in the bracket of wholly unreliable witness on whose deposition, the conviction cannot be based.

12. Further, regarding the age of the prosecutrix at the time of the alleged incident, although the prosecution has placed reliance upon school record vide Exh.24, the prosecution has not produced birth certificate or produced on record the ossification NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/466/2003 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/03/2026 undefined test report.
In the absence of such reliable evidence with regard to age, it cannot be held that the prosecutrix was a minor at the time of the alleged incident.

13. It is to be further noted that although the prosecutrix was six months pregnant at the time of lodging the complaint, the prosecution has not brought any evidence on record so as to establish the paternity of the child.
It also appears that no DNA test was conducted and also, the FSL report and Serological report does not connect the accused with the offence.

14. The Court may also draw strength from the decision of the Apex Court in case of Rajesh Prasad Vs. State of Bihar & Anr. reported in (2022) 3 SCC 471, wherein the Apex Court has examined the case law with regard to the power of the High Court to overturn the decision of the Sessions Court where another view is possible.

entities.text: Rajesh Prasad Vs. State of Bihar & Anr. reported in (2022) 3 SCC 471
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Examining the case including that of Chandrappa & Ors. vs. State of Karnataka reported in (2007) 4 SCC 415, the Apex Court has culled out the general principles regarding the powers of the Appellate Court while dealing with the appeal against the order of acquittal.

entities.text: Chandrappa & Ors. vs. State of Karnataka reported in (2007) 4 SCC 415
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court has held that the appellate court has full power to review, re-appreciate and reconsider the evidence upon which the order of acquittal is founded.

However, the appellate court has to keep in mind that in case of an acquittal, there is a double presumption in favour of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/466/2003 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/03/2026 undefined accused.

Firstly, the presumption of innocence is available to him under the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence, and thereafter, upon securing of acquittal, the presumption is further State Of Gujarat vs Jerabhai Lalabhai Thakore on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19238527/
5 reinforced, reaffirmed and strengthened, and therefore, whenever there are two reasonable conclusions are possible on the basis of the evidence on record, ordinarily, the Apex Court would not disturb the findings of acquittal recorded by the Trial court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
15. The Court can also draw strength from the judgment of the Apex Court in case of Nirmal Prekumar @ Anr. Vs. State represented by Inspector of Police, reported in (2024) 20 SCC, 293,
wherein the Apex Court has observed regarding weightage to be given to the testimony of a victim in matters involving sexual offences.

entities.text: Nirmal Prekumar @ Anr. Vs. State represented by Inspector of Police, reported in (2024) 20 SCC, 293
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In paras-19 and 20, the Apex Court observed as under:-
"19.

Before addressing the issues, we consider it appropriate to revisit the law laid down by this Court regarding the weight to be attached to the testimony of the victim in matters involving sexual offences where the prosecution's case hinges on the victim's evidence --a scenario central to the present case.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/466/2003 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/03/2026 undefined
The first two category of cases may not pose serious difficulty for the Court in arriving at its conclusion(s).

However, in the third category of cases, the Court has to be circumspect and look for corroboration of any material particulars by reliable testimony, direct or circumstantial, as a requirement of the rule of prudence."
16.

In the present case, considering the evidence of the prosecutrix, the Court finds it to be unreliable and finds that the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The Court therefore finds no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed by the trial Court.
17. In the result, the appeal fails and is dismissed.

The judgment and order dated 30.10.2002 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court No.2, Nadiad, District Kheda in Sessions case No.
155 of 1998 stands confirmed.
